turnos.plano: T1: split army to take Santarem (2cav+1arc, counter bonus) and Evora (1cav+3arc+2lan); kept 3 lanceiros guarding Lisboa. Built 1 cavaleiro (spent all 30w/30i). T2: both villages should be mine and producing. Push Santarem->Coimbra[3] or Badajoz[5]; Evora->Faro[6] or Badajoz[5]. Badajoz is the hub - decide with fresh scout info. Keep Lisboa building cav/arq each turn. Do NOT strip Lisboa bare again; do not chase Madrid yet.
turnos.dep: At dawn the banners left Lisboa in two columns - knights and archers on Santarem, the rest on Evora. Two villages, one morning, double the harvest. The King keeps three lances at home and a new knight in the forge. Portugal moves.
motor: REJEITADO: construir [0]: recurso insuficiente p/ cavaleiro (tem 30m/20f, custa 30m/30f)

turnos.plano: Capture Tarragona and Girona to expand territory. Build 2 lanceiros in Barcelona. Next turn, use new resources to produce arqueiros and reinforce captured villages. Plan to explore road network and target nearby villages.
turnos.dep: First turn as King B. Sending cavaleiros to seize neutral Tarragona and Girona. Building lanceiros to grow our forces. Hope to establish a foothold and expand the kingdom.
motor: placar: A 1 ald/tropas 3 | B 1 ald/tropas 9 | neutras 22 | transito 4 (A 2 | B 2)

turnos.plano: Goal: 18/24 villages. This turn: 2 cav Santarem->Badajoz (knight counters archer, 12v3, safe), 1 cav Evora->Faro (6v5, tight but wins, expect small loss). Lisboa built cav+arq (50w/40i paid). Next turn: Badajoz is a hub - look at Toledo[11]/Cordoba[10]/Salamanca[8] garrisons and hit the weakest; from Faro probe Sevilha[9]; new Lisboa troops + Santarem's 1 arq -> Coimbra[3] (needs >3 atk, 2 arq enough). Santarem/Evora should have 30w/20i by then - build there too. Do NOT mix lanceiros into an attack vs archers (counter trap). Don't strip capitals bare; keep 2-3 home each.
turnos.dep: At dawn the banners move: two knights ride west on Badajoz, one rides south on Faro, while Lisbon's forges hammer out a fresh knight and archer. Yesterday I held three villages - by week's end I mean to hold five. The map is wide, but it will be mine.

turnos.plano: Consolidate [17] and [18]. Reinforce new villages. Build arqueiros at Barcelona next turn.
turnos.dep: Bold move conquers Zaragoza and Huesca. Realm grows to 5 villages. King B expands.

turnos.plano: T3 strikes: Faro cav->Sevilha (6v5 win), Badajoz 2cav->Cordoba (12v8 win), Lisboa 3L+1A->Coimbra via Santarem (7.5v3, still wins if hardened to 5; arrives T5). Expect 8 villages by T5. Next turn: Badajoz+Faro get 30w/20i -> build arqueiros each turn, ship them to Cordoba; mass ~4 arqueiros then hit Toledo (lanceiros -> counter x1.5). After Coimbra falls, push Porto from there. Do NOT strip a capital to zero again - keep >=1 troop home. Enemy comes from NE; watch Madrid/Teruel/Murcia hubs. Hit neutrals before they harden.
turnos.dep: Three banners march at dawn: the knights of Badajoz ride on golden Cordoba, Faro's lone rider dares Sevilha, and Lisboa's spears walk north to Coimbra. While they bleed for me, every forge in my realm hammers out crossbows. Eight villages by week's end - the Reconquista has begun.

turnos.plano: Conquered four neutrals this turn. Capital retains troops for defense. Next: seize [22] Burgos and scout west.
turnos.dep: We push forward, claiming neutral soil. Each village brings us nearer to the 18-victory goal. King B's army grows.

turnos.plano: T5: Badajoz will have 3 arqueiros (1 built + 2 from Santarem) -> attack Salamanca (9 vs 5, arqueiros counter lanceiros). Cordoba gets Sevilha's knight -> build 1 arqueiro, T6 hit Toledo with 2C+1A (count tie breaks to arqueiro, ~18 vs 7.5). Enemy takes Madrid T5 - expect push at Cordoba/Salamanca/Toledo T6; Cordoba def ~7.5, accept risk. NEVER attack lanceiro garrisons with cavaleiro-only armies (their counter x1.5 beats me). After Porto falls, Coimbra rebuilds, later Vigo/Burgos lane. Evora+Lisboa are safe builders, keep stacking arqueiros.
turnos.dep: Three arrows leave my bow: Coimbra's spears march on Porto, Santarem's archers hurry to Badajoz, and Sevilha's lone knight rides to brace Cordoba. While they march, six archers and two spearmen take up arms across my lands. The enemy covets Madrid - let them bleed for it; I am forging the force that will seize Toledo and lock them out of the west.

turnos.plano: Turn 6: Badajoz has 5 arqueiros home + 6 arriving from Evora. Send 5 to Toledo (22.5 vs 10) and 5 to Salamanca (22.5 vs 8), keep the rest home. Cordoba: keep building arqueiros and send them to reinforce Madrid (1 turn away) - Madrid will hold only ~1 knight after attrition. NEVER attack Murcia with cavalry (lanceiros counter cavaleiros). Porto/Coimbra keep building arqueiros for Vigo later. Cordoba is nearly empty: if enemy retakes it, retake it from Madrid. Target: 12 villages by turn 7, then push Murcia/Valencia.
turnos.dep: Twelve villages is the prize, and I reach for it now. My two knights ride from Cordoba straight at Madrid before King B can catch his breath - twelve power against five, no hesitation. Evora's six archers march on Badajoz, where next turn they split and swallow Toledo and Salamanca. Eleven new archers rise across the realm this very night. The south is mine; now the center bleeds.

turnos.plano: T6: sent 2 cav Madrid->Zaragoza (12 eff vs 3, counter win) and 5 arc Badajoz->Toledo (15 vs 10). Built 14 troops. T7 plans: if Zaragoza fell, strike Burgos [22] from there (cav beats arq) or Teruel [20]; 6 arc arrive Badajoz t7 plus its 2 new lances - mass arcs there and hit Salamanca [8] (arcs counter lances); Cordoba will have 3 arcs -> send to Murcia [19] (2 med turns). NEVER send cav alone vs lanceiro garrisons (Toledo/Burgos lesson). Madrid sits empty until lances train - if enemy retakes it, recapture before pushing east.
turnos.dep: Madrid fell to me last night, and I do not pause to celebrate. My two knights thunder out of the empty city toward Zaragoza, while Badajoz's archers march on Toledo. Across ten villages, fourteen new soldiers take up arms. Two fronts advance at once - let King B wake to find his map shrinking.

turnos.plano: T7: three attacks - 2C Zaragoza>Huesca (12v3), 3A Toledo>Teruel (6v4.5), all Badajoz>Salamanca (21v8). Expect 15 villages. RISK taken: Zaragoza & Toledo empty for 1 turn - enemy passive so far, accept. Next turn: new 2C Zaragoza>Tarragona (12v5); Porto 1L+4A>Vigo (13.5v8); Cordoba 4A>Murcia arrives T9 (12v8); then cav vs Burgos (def 10). Do NOT blind-attack unseen 14/15/21 yet. Toledo has 0 res - rebuild next turn. Need 18 held 2 straight turns.
turnos.dep: Three blades leave the scabbard at once: knights thunder into Huesca, Toledo's archers march on Teruel, and Badajoz empties its halls into Salamanca. Behind them, every forge in the kingdom hammers through the night - and Zaragoza readies two more knights for the blow after next. King B hides behind thin walls. We knock.

turnos.plano: T9: took Vigo with Porto's 1L+4A (eff 15 v 8, archers counter lancers). Built archers everywhere; 3 knights at Huesca. Sent Madrid->Zaragoza (2L1A) and Santarem->Badajoz (4A) to patch the weak borders. T10: attack Pamplona [21] from Huesca with ALL 5 knights (~30 eff v ~10) - near-certain, then garrison it. T11: take Burgos [22] from Madrid or Zaragoza with 6+ archers (need att >= 10, no counter vs archers). Captures t9/t10/t11 -> hold 18 on t11+t12 = WIN. DON'T: touch Tarragona/Girona yet (def 18), don't strip Lisboa/Coimbra/Faro. Watch Zaragoza/Teruel/Badajoz - if enemy pushes, reinforce again. Murcia later with 6+ archers from Cordoba.
turnos.dep: While King B boasts of his conquest in Murcia, my banners march west - Porto's spears and bows descend on Vigo tonight, and by dawn it flies my colors. Across the realm every forge rings: forty archers rising in a single night, and three heavy knights waking in Huesca. My frontier is thin as parchment, but next moon Pamplona will learn whose king rules Iberia.

turnos.plano: T10 = arms race, ZERO attacks. All villages build arqueiros; Madrid 2A->Zaragoza, Salamanca 4A->Zaragoza, Toledo 2A->Madrid. Goal t11 safe borders: Zaragoza ~14 troops, Huesca 5C+3A, Teruel 9A, Cordoba 9A. T11: send Teruel 6A->Castellon (18 atk v 15 def, arq counters their lancers) + Zaragoza 2A->Huesca. T12: Huesca 2C+4A->Pamplona (16 v 10), keep 3C+4A home vs Girona. 18 villages at t13, then HOLD 2 straight turns, no new offensives till win. NEVER strip Huesca below ~3C+2A equiv; watch Barcelona sally via [13]/[14]; never split sends on one target.
turnos.dep: No blades drawn today - sixteen forges roar instead. While King B stares at my borders, eighty fresh arqueiros take shape, and Madrid and Salamanca march their gunpowder east to thicken Zaragoza. Let him blink first. When my line is iron, Castellon and Pamplona will fall in a single breath.

Murcia: 5 arq arrive T14 + 7 arq from Cordoba as second wave (each fights alone, both beat def 13). Sent 2 arq Huesca->Girona and built up all border villages. Do NOT strip Tarragona/Girona again until Barcelona is confirmed mine.
